bug_description.normalized: qpdf's DCT pipeline recovers an embedded progressive Huffman JPEG from the staged PDF and passes it to libjpeg-turbo. The recovered JPEG has three components, a first interleaved DC scan over components 1/2/3, and a later single-component Y AC scan with `Ss=1`, `Se=5`, `Ah=0`, `Al=2`. In the vulnerable `start_pass_phuff_decoder`, the first scan never initializes `prev_coef_bits`, so the later single-component scan leaves the Cb/Cr `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` entries undefined. `smoothing_ok()` copies those undefined entries into `prev_coef_bits_latch`, and `decompress_smooth_data()` reads them while evaluating `change_dc` on a later iMCU row, triggering the observed MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.description: First project-code read that creates vulnerability-relevant JPEG state: `get_sof()` pulls the component count from the recovered SOF header. For the staged witness this byte is `3`, which sizes the later `coef_bits` / `prev_coef_bits` tables and the all-component smoothing loops.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a PDF whose damaged image object 3 is recovered by qpdf into a Flate stream beginning at offset 2007. Trimming the bad checksum from that recovered stream yields a 463-byte JPEG that starts `ffd8...` and contains `SOF2`. `Pl_DCT::decompress()` passes that recovered JPEG buffer into libjpeg, and `get_sof()` reads `num_components = 3` from its SOF marker.

root_cause.code: for (coefi = MIN(cinfo->Ss, 1); coefi <= MAX(cinfo->Se, 9); coefi++) { if (cinfo->input_scan_number > 1) prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi] = coef_bit_ptr[coefi]; }
root_cause.description: On the first progressive Huffman scan, this loop has no `else` initialization for `prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi]` when `input_scan_number == 1`. The step therefore leaves each component's `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` undefined even though later block-smoothing code assumes those previous-scan entries are initialized. The fix patch adds `else prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi] = 0;` at this exact site; the recovered witness JPEG uses `SOF2`/`FFC4`, so the `jdphuff.c` side of the patch is the executed root cause.

sink.code: change_dc = coef_bits[1] == -1 && coef_bits[2] == -1 && coef_bits[3] == -1 && coef_bits[4] == -1 && coef_bits[5] == -1 && coef_bits[6] == -1 && coef_bits[7] == -1 && coef_bits[8] == -1 && coef_bits[9] == -1;
sink.description: MSAN sink. After `coef_bits` is redirected to the previous-scan latch for a later iMCU row, this `change_dc` test reads `coef_bits[1..9]`. For Cb/Cr on the witnessed path those latch entries carry the undefined `prev_coef_bits` values, producing the observed use-of-uninitialized-value at `jdcoefct.c:519`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports the first uninitialized use at `decompress_smooth_data /src/libjpeg-turbo/jdcoefct.c:519:26` and separately attributes the last store of the poisoned value to `smoothing_ok /src/libjpeg-turbo/jdcoefct.c:408:37`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This allocates the progression-status table for both current-scan `coef_bits` rows and previous-scan `prev_coef_bits` rows. The immediately following init loop at lines 668-670 writes `-1` only through the first `num_components * DCTSIZE2` entries, so the second half reserved for `prev_coef_bits` starts indeterminate until a later scan pass overwrites it.

parser_admitted.code: if (bad) ERREXIT4(cinfo, JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION, cinfo->Ss, cinfo->Se, cinfo->Ah, cinfo->Al);
parser_admitted.description: The recovered progressive Huffman scan headers satisfy the validation at this site, so the decoder does not raise `JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION` and instead enters the progression-status update loop on both scans. The witness headers are `scan0: n=3, comps={1,2,3}, Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1` and `scan1: n=1, comp={1}, Ss=1, Se=5, Ah=0, Al=2`.

coarse_trace.summary: qpdf hands the recovered DCT image stream from the staged PDF to libjpeg via `jpeg_buffer_src`, then starts JPEG header parsing and decompression.
The JPEG SOF parser reads a 3-component progressive image and populates component descriptors for component IDs 1, 2, and 3.
The JPEG SOS parser materializes the first interleaved DC scan over components 1/2/3 and the later single-component AC scan over component 1.
Because the recovered JPEG is progressive Huffman rather than arithmetic-coded, master selection initializes the progressive Huffman decoder and coefficient controller used by block smoothing.
The progressive Huffman decoder allocates a progression-status table with rows for both current and previous scans, but only the current-scan half is initialized.
The first scan leaves every component's `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` undefined, and the later single-component scan updates only the Y component's previous rows.
Block-smoothing setup copies the undefined Cb/Cr previous-coefficient bits into `prev_coef_bits_latch` and returns success, keeping the smoothing path enabled.
On a later iMCU row, smoothing aliases `coef_bits` to the previous-scan latch and reads the undefined Cb/Cr entries in `change_dc`, producing the observed MSAN uninitialized read.

fine_trace.note: Reads the SOF component count from the attacker-controlled JPEG header. For the recovered witness JPEG, this stores `3`, which determines the number of component descriptors, the size of `coef_bits`, and the later all-component smoothing iterations.

Allocates `comp_info[0..2]` and fills the SOF component table from the JPEG header. In the recovered witness, the loop at lines 282-289 records component IDs `1`, `2`, and `3`, which later let SOS parsing map scan component selectors back to Y/Cb/Cr.

fine_trace.var: cinfo->comps_in_scan, cinfo->cur_comp_info, cinfo->Ss, cinfo->Se, cinfo->Ah, cinfo->Al, cinfo->input_scan_number
fine_trace.note: Parses the first SOS marker. For the recovered witness JPEG, this SOS sets `n = 3`, maps `cur_comp_info[0..2]` to components `1/2/3`, stores `Ss = 0`, `Se = 0`, `Ah = 0`, `Al = 1`, and increments `input_scan_number` to `1`, defining an interleaved DC-first scan over all three components.

Master selection chooses progressive Huffman decoding and allocates `coef_bits` for both current-scan rows and previous-scan rows. The follow-on init loop only writes `-1` through the first `num_components * DCTSIZE2` integers, so the second half used as `prev_coef_bits` remains indeterminate at allocation time.

fine_trace.code: for (coefi = MIN(cinfo->Ss, 1); coefi <= MAX(cinfo->Se, 9); coefi++) { if (cinfo->input_scan_number > 1) prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi] = coef_bit_ptr[coefi]; }
fine_trace.note: Root cause on the first scan. Step 3 set `input_scan_number = 1`, so the guarded copy at lines 130-132 is skipped for every component and there is no default initialization of `prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi]`. The following loop only writes `coef_bit_ptr[0] = Al` for the DC band, leaving `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` undefined for Y, Cb, and Cr.

depends_on.via: cinfo->cur_comp_info, cinfo->Ss, cinfo->Se, cinfo->Ah, cinfo->Al, cinfo->input_scan_number

fine_trace.var: cinfo->comps_in_scan, cinfo->cur_comp_info, cinfo->Ss, cinfo->Se, cinfo->Ah, cinfo->Al, cinfo->input_scan_number
fine_trace.note: Parses the later SOS marker recovered from the witness JPEG. This scan sets `n = 1`, maps `cur_comp_info[0]` to component `1`, stores `Ss = 1`, `Se = 5`, `Ah = 0`, `Al = 2`, and increments `input_scan_number` to `2`, so only the Y component participates in this scan.

fine_trace.code: for (coefi = MIN(cinfo->Ss, 1); coefi <= MAX(cinfo->Se, 9); coefi++) { if (cinfo->input_scan_number > 1) prev_coef_bit_ptr[coefi] = coef_bit_ptr[coefi]; }
fine_trace.note: On the second scan, `input_scan_number > 1` is true, but step 6 made `comps_in_scan = 1`, so this loop executes only for component 1. It copies Y's current `coef_bits[1..9]` into Y's `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` and then writes `coef_bit_ptr[1..5] = 2`; the Cb/Cr `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` entries remain the undefined values left by step 5 because those components are absent from this scan.

depends_on.via: cinfo->cur_comp_info, cinfo->Ss, cinfo->Se, cinfo->Ah, cinfo->Al, cinfo->input_scan_number

fine_trace.note: With `input_scan_number = 2`, block-smoothing setup copies each component's `prev_coef_bits[1..9]` into `prev_coef_bits_latch[1..9]`. For Y the copied values are defined by step 7, but for Cb/Cr this statement stores the still-undefined `prev_coef_bits` entries into the previous-scan latch. The saved MSAN origin stack names this exact store site at `jdcoefct.c:408`.

Because block smoothing is enabled and `smoothing_ok(cinfo)` succeeds after step 8, output processing chooses `decompress_smooth_data()` instead of the non-smoothing path. This control decision is required for the later uninitialized read at line 519.

fine_trace.code: if (cinfo->output_iMCU_row > cinfo->master->last_good_iMCU_row) coef_bits = coef->coef_bits_latch + ((ci + cinfo->num_components) * SAVED_COEFS);
fine_trace.note: When output moves past the last good iMCU row, smoothing reads the previous-scan latch instead of the current-scan latch. Master selection initialized `last_good_iMCU_row` to `0` at `jdmaster.c:571`, and the staged fix description for this sample states the witness reached the second iMCU row with that value unchanged, so on the crashing path this branch aliases `coef_bits` to the previous-scan latch rows created in step 8.

fine_trace.code: change_dc = coef_bits[1] == -1 && coef_bits[2] == -1 && coef_bits[3] == -1 && coef_bits[4] == -1 && coef_bits[5] == -1 && coef_bits[6] == -1 && coef_bits[7] == -1 && coef_bits[8] == -1 && coef_bits[9] == -1;
fine_trace.note: Sink. With `coef_bits` redirected by step 10 to the previous-scan latch, this test reads the latched `coef_bits[1..9]` entries. For Cb/Cr on the witnessed path those entries came from the undefined `prev_coef_bits` values stored in step 8, so MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this exact predicate.

format.name: PDF with recovered progressive Huffman JPEG stream
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is a PDF whose image object 3 recovers to a Flate-decoded progressive Huffman JPEG (`SOF2`, `FFC4`) with `num_components = 3`, a first SOS `n=3` over components `1/2/3` with `Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1`, and a later SOS `n=1` over component `1` with `Ss=1, Se=5, Ah=0, Al=2`, so libjpeg-turbo reaches block smoothing with undefined Cb/Cr `prev_coef_bits[1..9]`.
